conventions.deferred:: A real obligation this plan carries; the suffix names the milestone whose scope in PLAN.md the clause falls in — S4 for sessions, links and flow control, whose scope line names handle allocation, link resumption, link errors and forced detach. The note names the gap that keeps the clause out of the carrier set. An entry with this value says that nothing under lean/ or vectors/ carries the clause's requirement: a missing carrier is recorded rather than covered by naming a declaration that does not hold the rule.
conventions.formalized:: A Lean declaration path that carries this clause's meaning. Every path recorded here is a declaration the module it names actually holds, and the ledger's existence gate resolves it against lean/** rather than taking this note's word for it; where the carrier is only part of the clause, the note names the half it does not carry.
conventions.kind: The clause's own keyword, read from the ledger's clause rather than inferred from the coverage class: the class is MUST for both forms, so kind and class diverge for MUST NOT; the two MUST NOT clauses of this family (`links.31`, `doc:flow-control.9`) are marked MUST NOT here, and the rest are MUST.
conventions.superseded:: Decided by an entry in the ambiguity register under ledger/ambiguities, whose id is the suffix. The entry's own clause list must name this clause, which is what makes the citation a decision rather than a reference to neighbouring material.
conventions.uncarried: No declaration and no vector carries the clause's requirement. A declaration that only recognises the vocabulary a clause is written in — reading a field without acting on it — is not a carrier; where one of those exists the note names it as the near-miss so a reader can see why it was not counted, and a finding is stated where the model admits what the clause forbids.

design_consequences: This file holds all thirty-two must-class clauses of the `links` family: the seventeen of the anchor and the fifteen of its three child docs (`doc:flow-control` 7, `doc:resuming-deliveries` 7, `doc:closing-a-link` 1). Twenty-three are uncarried and say so, eight are carried by declarations in the session layer with the case each misses named in its note, and one is decided by the register.

Uncarried (deferred:S4), twenty-three: the anchor's .1, .2, .4, .5, .7, .8, .10, .13, .16, .17, .18, .23; `doc:flow-control`'s .4, .7, .11; all seven of `doc:resuming-deliveries`; and `doc:closing-a-link`.2. They are the same object seen from every side: the model has one link per session with a handle registry (lean/Spec/Session.lean:446-448) and no link name, no terminus properties, no unsettled map, no link-error family, no read of the attach's `unsettled` or the transfer's `resume`, and no sending side. Twenty-three clauses, one shape.

Carried, eight: .14 by `detachLink`'s release (the destruction; the error case and any record of it are the gap), .15 by `linkHandleOf` and the placement in `step` (the handle half; the delivery-ids half is not carried), .22 by `transferLink`'s first-transfer requirement (that a tag is present, not who chose it), .33 by `transferLink`'s abort branch (the delivery's record, because a payload is opaque here), and the flow-control doc's .2, .3, .5 and .9 by the credit arithmetic — `Position.creditFor`, its use in `flowLink` and `transferLink`, and the state law `SenderCreditState`. Those four are the family's well-covered corner: the credit is the one per-link quantity the model keeps, and its clauses are the ones that have both a declaration and a vector.

Decided by the register: .31, by `interleaved-deliveries-absorbed`, whose clause list names it and whose adopted reading — the second delivery's first transfer absorbed as a continuation — is what `transferLink`'s continuation branch implements. The entry is the reason no carrier is owed: the clause constrains the sender, and the artifact says nothing about a receiver's answer to a peer that interleaves.

Three clauses are vacuous in this model rather than missing, for the same single-link, single-delivery shape: .1's name uniqueness and .23's delivery-tag uniqueness, because only one link and one delivery exist at a time, and `doc:flow-control.4`'s assumption, which the model answers with a zero rather than with the count the sentence names, indistinguishably under the flow rule's own count check. That shape is what `interleaved-deliveries-absorbed` and `link-uniqueness-vacuous` record; neither entry's clause list names these clauses, so neither is cited, and widening either is the planner's decision.

The nearest neighbour of `links.2` is implemented and is a different clause: `attachLink` refuses an attach whose handle is already claimed (lean/Spec/Session.lean:686-689) under `attach/field:handle.2`, where `links.2` says a second attach for a non-suspended link may succeed and the first attach be closed with `link-error`. A register entry would be the record if the model ever expresses stealing; today the model cannot ask the question.

`links.4` is the family's one behavioural finding: an inbound attach whose terminus is null is admitted and keeps its link, where the sentence requires the newly created endpoint to be detached. `links.13`, `.16`, `.17`, `.18`, the resumption doc and the closing-a-link doc are the same missing object seen from further sides — the error detach that is never built, the reattach that cannot be forbidden because a resume cannot be recognised, the `unsettled` field that is never read, the pipelined attach that cannot be told from either, the seven sentences about unsettled maps the session does not hold, and the closing detach whose `closed` flag is never read.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: Link names MUST uniquely identify the link amongst all links of the same direction between the two participating containers.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: deferred: S4 — uncarried: the model stores no link name and holds one link per session, so the uniqueness this sentence requires has no subject. `attachLink` (lean/Spec/Session.lean:656-736) reads an attach's role, handle, initial-delivery-count, snd-settle-mode and target and never its `name`, and the session keeps one handle registry for its one link (lean/Spec/Session.lean:446-448). This is the shape the register calls vacuous for `sessions.1` (`link-uniqueness-vacuous`), but that entry's text and clause list name `sessions.1` alone, so it is not cited here; widening it, or registering a name-uniqueness reading, is the planner's pen.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: In this case, the endpoint MUST send a «detach» frame to inform the remote peer that the handle is no longer attached to the link endpoint.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: deferred: S4 — uncarried: the sentence obliges the endpoint to send a frame, and no declaration builds one — the corpus supplies every frame and the model transitions on the frames it is given, which is the gap `connections.5`'s entry records for the close frame. Near-miss: `detachLink`'s outbound branch releases this endpoint's output handle (lean/Spec/Session.lean:944-957), so the unmapping the sentence announces is modelled; what is absent is any policy that decides to unmap, and the vector that exercises a release, `exchange-link-detach-releases-handle`, is a *received* detach.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: When an error occurs at a link endpoint, the endpoint MUST be detached with appropriate error information supplied in the error field of the «detach» frame.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: deferred: S4 — uncarried: the sentence obliges the endpoint to build a detach carrying the error, and no declaration builds a frame — the corpus supplies every frame and the model transitions on the ones it is given, the gap `connections.5`'s entry records for the close frame. Near-miss: the receiving half of the same idea is read, not produced — `detachLink`'s own docstring says a detach carrying an `error` ends the link with that error, whose details the layer 'carries rather than judges' (lean/Spec/Session.lean:936-943) — and nothing retains the error afterwards, which `Contracts/Settlement.lean`'s closing section records as a model with no per-link error field.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: The link endpoint MUST then be destroyed.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: formalized:SpecAMQP.Spec.Session.detachLink — the release is the destruction: it clears the endpoint's handle, role, flow state and delivery (lean/Spec/Session.lean:944-957), and a later frame naming that handle is refused as unattached (`linkHandleOf`, lean/Spec/Session.lean:608-625). The case this misses, stated as a finding: the destruction is not conditioned on an error and nothing about the error survives it, so the sentence's 'then' — destroyed after the error detach of `.13` — reads here as destroyed by any detach. `Contracts/Settlement.lean`'s closing section records the field a model distinguishing the two would need.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: If any input (other than a detach) related to the endpoint either via the input handle or delivery-ids be received, the session MUST be terminated with an «errant-link» session-error.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: formalized:SpecAMQP.Spec.Session.linkHandleOf; formalized:SpecAMQP.Spec.Session.step; test:exchange-link-detach-releases-handle — input naming a handle that is not the attached link is refused with the `session-error` family's `unattached-handle`, read from the generated table (lean/Spec/Session.lean:608-625), and `step` places a link-level refusal in the DISCARDING phase that ends the session when the peer's end arrives (lean/Spec/Session.lean:1222-1229); the vector pins the released case, a transfer naming a handle its link no longer has. Two gaps, stated as findings: the delivery-ids half of the sentence is not carried — nothing relates a delivery-id to a link, so input that names a destroyed endpoint only by delivery-id is not refused by this rule — and the model keeps no state for an endpoint destroyed with an error as against one released, so the two read alike (`Contracts/Settlement.lean`).

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: Since the link endpoint has been destroyed, the peer cannot reattach, and MUST resume the link in order to restore communication.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: deferred: S4 — uncarried: the sentence both forbids a reattach and requires a resume, and the model can express neither. With no link name, no terminus and no read of the attach's `unsettled` field (`.17`), an attach after a release that names a fresh handle is admitted by `attachLink` (lean/Spec/Session.lean:656-736) and creates a new link rather than restoring one, so there is no distinction between reattaching and resuming to enforce. The restriction `interleaved-deliveries-absorbed` records — one held delivery, no link registry — is the same shape: a resume would have to restore into something the session does not keep.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: In order to disambiguate the resume request from a pipelined re-attach the resuming «attach» performative MUST contain a non-null value for its unsettled field.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: deferred: S4 — uncarried: nothing reads the attach's `unsettled` field, which is the whole of the discriminator this sentence names. `attachLink` (lean/Spec/Session.lean:656-736) reads an attach's role, handle, initial-delivery-count, snd-settle-mode and target, and the session holds one delivery in progress (`Session.delivery`, lean/Spec/Session.lean:464) rather than a map of unsettled deliveries, so a non-null value has nothing to be true of. This is `.5`'s gap read from the resuming side: the same field, required to be absent-to-present in one case and present in the other.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: Receipt of a pipelined «attach» MUST result in the session being terminated with an «errant-link» session-error.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: deferred: S4 — uncarried: with no link name, no terminus and no `unsettled` read (`.16`, `.17`), a pipelined attach is indistinguishable from a resume, so the model cannot recognise the input this sentence answers. Near-miss: the one re-attach the model does refuse is a second attach on a handle already claimed, and that refusal is `attachLink`'s `handleInUse` branch (lean/Spec/Session.lean:686-689), which is `attach/field:handle.2`'s immediate connection close, not this sentence's termination of the session with a session-error.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: If an attempt is made to attach the link subsequently when it is not suspended, then the link can be 'stolen', i.e., the second attach succeeds and the first attach MUST then be closed with a link error of «stolen».
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: deferred: S4 — uncarried: nothing carries the stealing rule. The nearest behaviour is the opposite clause's: `attachLink` refuses an attach whose handle is already claimed with an immediate close carrying `handle-in-use` (lean/Spec/Session.lean:686-689), which is `attach/field:handle.2`, while this sentence says a second attach for a non-suspended link succeeds and the first attach is closed with `link-error`. The model has no link-error family, no link-name identity to steal under and no second-attach path, so which of the two applies is not a question it can ask.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: Each delivery MUST be identified by a delivery-tag chosen by the sending application.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: formalized:SpecAMQP.Spec.Session.transferLink — the first transfer of a delivery must carry its `delivery-tag` and `message-format` (lean/Spec/Session.lean:842-847, refused as `invalid-field`/`malformed`), and the tag the first transfer carried is what the delivery is recorded under for the rest of its life (lean/Spec/Session.lean:479, :890-892), so a continuation is identified by the same tag. What the model cannot carry is the sentence's 'chosen by the sending application': who chose the tag is not observable on the wire. No `test:` is claimed: the corpus's discriminating case for a tagless transfer, `exchange-link-first-transfer-needs-its-fields`, refuses for the tag and the format together and cites the transfer field clauses, so it does not isolate this sentence's rule.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: The delivery-tag MUST be unique amongst all deliveries that could be considered unsettled by either end of the link.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: deferred: S4 — uncarried, and vacuous in this model rather than missing: at most one delivery is ever in flight — `Session.delivery` is a single optional delivery (lean/Spec/Session.lean:464), cleared when the delivery completes or is aborted (lean/Spec/Session.lean:873, :875-889) — so no two deliveries can be unsettled at once and uniqueness has no pair to constrain. A tag may be reused by a later delivery, but never concurrently. This is the restriction `interleaved-deliveries-absorbed` records for `.31` and `link-uniqueness-vacuous` records for sessions.1; neither entry's clause list names this clause, so neither is cited. The register would be the record if the session ever held a delivery map.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: However, messages transferred along a single link MUST NOT be interleaved.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: superseded:interleaved-deliveries-absorbed — the register's decision, with its evidence: a probe found three transfers interleaving two deliveries on one link admitted step-for-step by both artefacts over 21 verdicts, and the reading adopted is that the second delivery's first transfer is absorbed as a continuation of the delivery in progress, the session keeping the *first* delivery's id. That is `transferLink`'s continuation branch (lean/Spec/Session.lean:815-921, where a transfer's id and identity fields are read from the held delivery), and the entry's own words are why no carrier is owed for the prohibition: the clause constrains the sender, and refusing loudly would be inventing a receiver behaviour the artifact does not state.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: In this case the receiver MUST discard the message data that was transferred prior to the abort.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: formalized:SpecAMQP.Spec.Session.transferLink — a transfer that carries `aborted` releases the delivery rather than continuing it (lean/Spec/Session.lean:868-875), so what the receiver discards is the delivery's record: a transfer's payload is opaque to this layer, which is why the sentence's 'message data' is carried as the delivery it belonged to. The corpus's abort vector, `exchange-link-aborted-discarded`, is the nearest evidence and is named rather than claimed as a `test:` witness: its cited clauses are `transfer/field:aborted.1` and `.2`, where the same rule is stated as a SHOULD.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: In this case, the session endpoint MUST immediately detach the newly created link endpoint.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: deferred: S4 — uncarried: no declaration reads an attach's local terminus (source or target), so a peer that declined to create one is indistinguishable from a peer that supplied one. `attachLink` (lean/Spec/Session.lean:656-736) creates the link endpoint for any attach it admits, and its only read of `target` is the coordinator recognition at `Session.withControlLink` (lean/Spec/Session.lean:573-580). Finding: an inbound attach whose terminus is null — how the artifact says a peer declines, and also what the recovery case of `links.u5` leaves in the field — is admitted and keeps its link, where this sentence requires the newly created endpoint to be detached.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: If either end of the link is already associated with a terminus, the «attach» frame MUST include its unsettled delivery state.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: deferred: S4 — uncarried: the attach's `unsettled` field is read nowhere, and the model holds no unsettled delivery state to put in it. The fields `attachLink` reads are those listed under `.1`; the session's one delivery (lean/Spec/Session.lean:464) is a delivery in progress rather than a map of unsettled deliveries, which `Contracts/Settlement.lean`'s closing section records. The subject of the sentence does not exist in the model, so it is uncarried rather than unimplemented, and it is the resumption family's — `links.17`'s non-null `unsettled` for a resuming attach has the same gap.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: In this case the endpoint MUST report the actual properties of the terminus as created.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: deferred: S4 — uncarried: the model holds no terminus properties, so there is nothing whose actual properties could differ from the expected ones this sentence contrasts with. `attachLink` (lean/Spec/Session.lean:656-736) validates the handle, the role and the delivery-count a sender announces and installs no source or target: the attach's `source` field is never read, and `target` is read only to recognise a coordinator (lean/Spec/Session.lean:573-580).

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: Note that a peer MUST take responsibility for verifying that the remote terminus meets its requirements.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: deferred: S4 — uncarried: the obligation is over a remote terminus's requirements and the model holds no terminus to have them. The nearest behaviour is the artifact's own instance of the same idea rather than a carrier for this sentence: `declare`'s `global-id` rule refuses a declare whose coordinator announced no `distributed-transactions` capability (lean/Spec/Transactions.lean:292-296), which is a field rule dispositioned with the `global-id` clauses. The general responsibility — that a peer verifies rather than assumes — is stated nowhere.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: In this case, the partner MUST signal that it has closed the link by reattaching and then sending a closing detach.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: deferred: S4 — uncarried: the partner's half of the closing exchange has no carrier. `detachLink` reads the detach's `handle` and nothing else (lean/Spec/Session.lean:944-957): it never reads the `closed` flag, so a non-closing detach and a closing one are the same frame to it, and the model has no reattach-with-a-closing-detach signal to send — the sending side is absent for the reason `links.10` gives. Near-miss: the vector `exchange-link-detach-unattached-handle` cites this anchor's `.1`, the MAY this sentence answers, and pins a detach naming a handle this endpoint does not have being admitted — the exception `links.15` reserves for detaches.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: If the sender's drain flag is set and there are no available messages, the sender MUST advance its delivery-count until link-credit is zero, and send its updated «flow» state to the receiver.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: deferred: S4 — uncarried: the rule is an action the model has no site for — a sender advancing its delivery-count to consume the credit and then sending its updated state — and the model has no sending side at all, so the frame half of the sentence has nowhere to live (the gap `connections.5`'s entry records for the close frame). Near-miss: `flowLink` reads `drain` only as a field whose presence is forbidden without a handle (lean/Spec/Session.lean:752-763), and both contracts record the omission — `Contracts/SessionCredit.lean` closes with '`drain`'s direction-dependent meaning ... is not modelled because nothing in the slice reads it', and `Contracts/FlowControl.lean` records that `drain` moves none of the window quantities.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: The sender's value MUST always be maintained in such a way as to match the delivery-limit identified by the receiver.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: formalized:SpecAMQP.Spec.Session.Position.creditFor; formalized:SpecAMQP.Proofs.SessionCredit.SenderCreditState; test:exchange-link-credit-echoed — a sender's credit is not a quantity it maintains but whatever the receiver's pair leaves room for: `Position.creditFor` is the equation (lean/Spec/Session.lean:380-389) and `flowLink`'s sender branch rebuilds the credit with it where a flow arrives (lean/Spec/Session.lean:786-795). The state law is `SenderCreditState` (lean/Proofs/SessionCredit.lean:67-69), with `SenderCreditState.invariant` re-exporting the equation (:71-72) and the initial and frame cases discharged (:75, :84). The case it misses is stated in both files rather than glossed: the three operation lemmas for the transitions that move the quantities are not proved — the module names them, and `Contracts/SessionCredit.lean` records that no acceptance declaration may take the invariant from it until they exist — so the law is stated and true by construction for two of its five obligations, not proved. The vector cites this clause and pins the deviation the ownership sentence forbids: a sender's flow naming a credit the receiver did not send.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: This means that the sender's link-credit variable MUST be set according to this formula when flow information is given by the receiver:
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: formalized:SpecAMQP.Spec.Session.Position.creditFor; test:exchange-link-credit-regranted; test:exchange-link-attach-keeps-the-credit — the sentence's formula, `link-credit_snd := delivery-count_rcv + link-credit_rcv - delivery-count_snd`, is `Position.creditFor` (lean/Spec/Session.lean:380-389), applied at the one site a flow reaches a sender (lean/Spec/Session.lean:786-795), and the subtraction is over the naturals so a receiver whose numbers leave no room grants zero rather than a negative credit the doc does not describe. Both vectors cite this clause: one raises the receiver's credit and shows the sender's rise by the same amount, the other shows the equation surviving an attach that does not re-establish the link.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: In the event that the receiver does not yet know the delivery-count, i.e., delivery-count rcv is unspecified, the sender MUST assume that the delivery-count rcv is the first delivery-count snd sent from sender to receiver, i.e., the delivery-count snd specified in the flow state carried by the initial «attach» frame from the sender to the receiver.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: deferred: S4 — uncarried: the assumption this sentence states is a value the model does not compute. It requires a sender whose receiver has not announced a delivery-count to take that count as the sender's own initial count; the model's sender reads the receiver's count from `peerCount`, which is zero until a flow announces one, and a freshly established link is therefore a sender with nothing to spend — a choice `Contracts/SessionCredit.lean`'s initialisation bullet records as deliberate ('the right side is `0 + 0 - initialDeliveryCount`, which truncates to zero'). Near-miss: `attachLink` adopts a partner's announced `initial-delivery-count` into `peerCount` (lean/Spec/Session.lean:718-733), which is the same quantity read from the other end, and it is that adoption `.5` and `.9` are about rather than this assumption. The two readings coincide wherever the model's flow rule admits a flow, because `flowCountRefusal?` (lean/Spec/Session.lean:632-654) requires a flow's delivery-count to be the one this endpoint already holds, so no vector distinguishes them.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: Additionally, whenever the sender increases delivery-count, it MUST decrease link-credit by the same amount in order to maintain the delivery-limit identified by the receiver.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: formalized:SpecAMQP.Spec.Session.transferLink — the transfer that begins a delivery moves both quantities in one record: `credit := current.credit - 1` and `deliveryCount := current.deliveryCount + 1` (lean/Spec/Session.lean:905-916), which is this sentence's 'by the same amount' as arithmetic rather than as an invariant. No vector cites this clause; `exchange-link-credit-granted-and-spent` pins the gate the same branch implements under `doc:flow-control.9`, and the conservation theorem `Position.creditFor_succ` (lean/Spec/Session.lean:391-394) is the fact that the two moves keep the equation true.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: If this happens, the receiver MUST maintain a floor of zero in its calculation of the value of available.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: deferred: S4 — uncarried: `available` is read nowhere as a quantity. The model holds no receiver-side calculation of it — `Session` carries the link's delivery-count and credit as `position` (lean/Spec/Session.lean:455) and the partner's announced pair as `peerCount` and `peerCredit` (lean/Spec/Session.lean:457-458), and nothing else — so there is no floor for the sentence to be a floor of. Near-miss: `flowLink` reads `available` only as a field whose presence is forbidden without a handle (lean/Spec/Session.lean:752-763), which is `flow/field:available.1`'s rule, and `Contracts/SessionCredit.lean`'s closing section records that `available` is outside that contract because the model holds no sender-side quantity for a receiver to echo.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: If the link-credit is less than or equal to zero, i.e., the delivery-count is the same as or greater than the delivery-limit, a sender MUST NOT send more messages.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: formalized:SpecAMQP.Spec.Session.transferLink; test:exchange-link-credit-granted-and-spent; test:exchange-link-credit-counts-messages-not-frames — the gate is one guard in the transfer's sender branch, `refuseUnless (!starting || current.credit > 0)` (lean/Spec/Session.lean:905-910), refused as `amqp:connection:framing-error` with the `limit` class because the credit is a bound the receiver set; a continuation transfer of a delivery already counted is admitted without credit, which is what makes the second vector discriminating — the credit counts messages, not frames.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: If the sending application marks the resend attempt as a resumed delivery then it MUST be ignored by the receiver.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: deferred: S4 — uncarried: nothing reads the `resume` flag, which is the whole of the discriminator this sentence turns on. `transferLink` reads the transfer's delivery-id, delivery-tag, message-format, settled, more and aborted (lean/Spec/Session.lean:819-921) and no `resume`; the session holds one delivery rather than a map of unsettled ones (`Session.delivery`, lean/Spec/Session.lean:464), which is the restriction `Contracts/Settlement.lean:185-189` records for exactly this family — 'the clauses that talk about *entries* — resumption, in-doubt resolution, `unsettled`'s completeness — have no state to range over'. amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: Deliveries in this category MUST be resumed by the sender.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: deferred: S4 — uncarried: 'resumed by the sender' is an action over the source's unsettled map, and the model holds one delivery in progress rather than a map of them (lean/Spec/Session.lean:464), so there is nothing to resume. No declaration reads the transfer's `resume` field (`.8`) and none records a delivery tag across deliveries, which is what a resume would be keyed on.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: In this case the two endpoints MUST reduce the levels of unsettled state as much as they can by the sender resuming and/or settling transfers that it observes that the receiver considers unsettled.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: deferred: S4 — uncarried: the sentence's quantity — the *levels* of unsettled state at the two ends, to be reduced by resuming and settling what the other side still holds — has no representation. The session holds one delivery and no map from delivery-tags to states (lean/Spec/Session.lean:464; `Contracts/Settlement.lean:185-189`), so there is no level to reduce, and the reduce-and-suspend cycle this sentence begins is not modelled either.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: Upon completion of this reduction of state, the two parties MUST suspend and re-attempt to resume the link.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: deferred: S4 — uncarried: the model has no suspend-and-resume cycle — an attach after a release creates a fresh link rather than restoring one (see `links.16`), and nothing distinguishes a resume from a re-attach because the attach's `unsettled` field is read nowhere (`links.17`). The sentence is the second half of the reduction `.6` states, and both are over state the session does not hold.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: The resume flag of the «transfer» frame MUST be set to true when resuming a delivery.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: deferred: S4 — uncarried: the `resume` flag is read nowhere, as in `.2`, so a resuming transfer is not distinguishable from a continuing one. Near-miss worth naming precisely: the model does carry the *interpretation* of the neighbouring flag — `Delivery.step` accumulates `settled` across a delivery's transfers (lean/Spec/Session.lean:405-414) — which shows the shape a `resume` reader would take, and nothing reads `resume`.
